solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: From time to time, they opted to advertise extravagantly

indicators.note: something done only from time to time happens at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A group occasionally chose to promote something over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype something is to promote or publicise it with exaggerated claims.

clue.text: Very fine hotel and travel company

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a company that carries travellers by plane

explanation.surface: Praise for a splendid hotel and the firm that flew you there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very fine' reads as praise for the hotel, but it is the definition, in the sense of very thin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or margin is an extremely thin or narrow one, as thin as a single hair.

clue.text: Every year has confused former governor

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year
the three letters of this word, jumbled

explanation.surface: An old governor is muddled every year.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking official, such as a provincial governor, in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Stick-in-the-mud is around, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting that a dull, old-fashioned person is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is figuratively a person stuck in outdated ways, just as a stick-in-the-mud resists change.

clue.text: Owing primarily to being empathetic, dad notices I'm upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read from bottom to top
primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.words: to being empathetic, dad notices I'm
parts.note: the opening letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A father, sensing his child is distressed, responds with empathy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of six words, then read upwards, give IN DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone owing money has borrowed and not yet repaid it, which is being in debt.

clue.text: Obvious thing most shops do every day?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a case so clear it needs no argument

definitions.text: thing most shops do every day
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a shop unlocks in the morning and closes in the evening

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is straightforward and easily settled, with an outcome that is plain to everyone.

clue.text: Cut area above part of the nose

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for area
the bony ridge at the top of the nose

explanation.surface: A surgeon's note about an incision just over the bridge of the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' places the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, a verb meaning to cut it down.

clue.text: Wedding ceremony maybe just announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound and spelt differently

parts.note: just means fair or proper; the word for that sounds identical

explanation.surface: A wedding has only just been made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only recently', but it means right, as in fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal ritual, and a wedding is one example of such a ceremony.

clue.text: Trendy drink I ultimately considered bland

parts.note: fashionable things are said to be in
a small mouthful
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a fashionable cocktail as tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insipid lacks flavour or interest, a close synonym of bland.

clue.text: A pretty cold, rampant creature from a long time ago

definitions.text: creature from a long time ago

indicators.note: rampant suggests wild, unchecked growth, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: all eleven letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty cold is spreading wildly, like a prehistoric beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The pterodactyl was a flying reptile that lived in the age of the dinosaurs, millions of years back.

clue.text: Bird heading west in winter, generally

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftward, so the letters are read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bird that tends to fly west in winter, like a migrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests migration, but both 'heading west' and 'in' are instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird of marshes and shores.

clue.text: Good players on course to be seen here?

definitions.text: Good players on course to be seen here?

parts.note: surface reading: skilled sportspeople heading for success

parts.words: on course to be seen here?
parts.note: setter's reading: on a golf course, the best scorers are displayed on a large board

explanation.walkthrough: 'On course' reads as heading the right way, but it is literally a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaderboard is the scoreboard showing the top-ranked competitors in a golf tournament.

clue.text: Experiment covering every single box with leaves

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: a trial
each means every single one

explanation.surface: A scientist runs a trial on every single box containing plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests plant foliage; here they are tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box used to ship tea leaves, later used for moving house.

clue.text: One overwhelmed by morally unacceptable idea

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed by it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: 'not on' is British idiom for unacceptable behaviour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single person swamped by a wicked idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is British slang for not acceptable, as in 'that's just not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, a common synonym for an idea.

clue.text: Attempt to take on old play such as Romeo and Juliet

definitions.text: play such as Romeo and Juliet

indicators.note: to take on is to take in or absorb, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a go or effort
aged means old

explanation.surface: An actor makes a bid to tackle a classic Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet ends with both lovers dead, making it a classic example of Shakespearean tragedy.

clue.text: Stick plug in this spot

parts.note: to plug a product is to advertise it; AD is short for advertisement
here means at this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a plug into a socket right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' looks like an electrical item, but it is a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling firmly to a surface, as glue does when it sticks.

clue.text: Valuable things, like complete collections

parts.note: as means in the manner of
a full set is a complete collection

explanation.surface: Full sets of collectables are treasured possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are items of value owned by a person or business, such as property or savings.

clue.text: I can see that, strangely, this can cause numbness

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd fashion, so the letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: all eleven letters of these four words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notices an odd effect that could leave them without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: ANAESTHETIC is the British spelling; Americans write anesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic is a drug given to remove sensation, so it numbs pain.

clue.text: Top scores sometimes given just before the end — this could be perfect

parts.note: a perfect mark out of ten, as judges sometimes award

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: Judges sometimes hand out maximum marks right at the close of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' seems to describe a score, but it is the grammatical perfect tense, as in 'I have eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is a grammatical tense, so a tense is the category it belongs to.

clue.text: A scrap of cloth put over jelly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: put over suggests flipping something, so in this down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rag is a torn scrap of fabric

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric laid over a dish of jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used as a jelly in labs and cooking.

clue.text: Guy outside hospital somewhere in Belgium

indicators.note: outside means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a guy is a man, a gent
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A man waits outside a hospital in a Belgian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghent is a historic city in Flanders, a place in Belgium.

clue.text: Friendly agreement two medical departments broke in the end

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department, taken twice

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: Two hospital departments finally broke off an amicable deal.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the hospital unit for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale between Britain and France.

clue.text: Solitary, dancing Queen fan?

indicators.note: dancing makes things move about, so the letters change places

parts.note: all eight letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone fan of the band Queen dancing to Dancing Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen fan' evokes the rock band (and the ABBA song 'Dancing Queen'), but it means a supporter of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist supports the monarchy, so they are a fan of the Queen or King.

clue.text: Opening part of athletics meet failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter does not appear, so the word loses its head

parts.note: a race or field contest at a meeting

explanation.surface: The start of an athletics meeting is a washout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the start of the meet, but it is the definition, a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an aperture letting air or gas escape, so it is a kind of opening.
